native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Across the ten most widespread habitat types inventoried in the Barcelona province, the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies markedly with habitat type: it is highest in Wetlands (55.8% of non-native occurrences; 29 of 52; per-plot median gardening share 0.75, IQR 0.25–1.00) and Coastal habitats (53.5%; 23 of 43; median 0.50, IQR 0.31–0.85), and lowest in Croplands (18.5%; 20 of 108; median 0.00, IQR 0.00–0.33), where the unintentional pathway dominates (76.9%). Urban plots show only ~30% gardening prevalence (45 of 151), despite being the prototypical gardening-pressure habitat, because unintentional introductions are the majority there as well. Pathway composition differs very significantly across habitats (chi-squared = 75.20, df = 18, p approximately 5.8e-9); permutation tests on the spread of pooled gardening prevalence across the 10 habitats are essentially indistinguishable from zero (p = 0.0001 for both range and variance statistics over 9999 label shuffles). Four habitats (Broad-leaved forests, Coniferous forests, Scrublands, Rock outcrops) have fewer than 10 non-native occurrences summed across plots and their apparent prevalences are unreliable, flagged separately. At the species level, gardening-introduced species (n=39 after removing 4 duplicates) occupy a median of 2 habitat types (IQR 1-3) and a median of 2 invaded plots (IQR 1-5), broadly similar to but not exceeding unintentional-introduced species in breadth.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots, 10 habitats) as the primary table. For each habitat, computed pooled prevalence p_gard(h) = sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) and the per-plot proportion r = n.gard/n.total (excluding plots with n.total == 0), reporting median and IQR. Ranked habitats by p_gard and flagged low-n habitats (sum n.total < 10). Ran a chi-squared test of independence on the pathway x habitat contingency of pooled plot-level counts (3 pathways x 10 habitats). Ran a permutation test shuffling habitat labels among plots for 9999 shuffles, with both range and variance of p_gard as test statistics. Used invasion_success_pathways.csv only as a secondary cross-reference, deduplicated species by Scientific_name (4 duplicates removed), and reported median (IQR) of habitat.range and number.of.invaded.plots by intro.pathway. Temporal / land-cover covariates (1956-2009) were not used; phylogeny was not used.
